concerns.text: The metric *translation_error* is defined as a binary mismatch against a *deterministic greedy reference plan* (FR‑008). This reference plan is itself produced by a heuristic (greedy cost‑based algorithm) rather than a true ground‑truth execution plan. Consequently, the validation claim in H2 – that translation‑error rate remains stable across complexity – measures stability of agreement with a model, not actual correctness of the router’s plans. Treating this heuristic‑derived plan as “ground truth” creates a circular validation: the predictor (reference plan) and the outcome (translation_error) are definitionally linked, so the analysis can only ever confirm the heuristic’s internal consistency, not an empirical property of the system.
